newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: TIBS in US$75.6 mln China joint venture.
newsitem.headline: TIBS in US$75.6 mln China joint venture.

text.p: Bus company TIBS Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it had agreed to set up a joint venture company in China with a state-owned company to design and make coach chassis and trucks.

TIBS said in a statement the initial total investment value of the joint venture company, to be owned 50:50 by it and Dandong Automobile Works (DAW) of China's Liaoning Province, would be US$75.6 million.
The registered capital of the company was expected to be US$36 million, it said.

TIBS and DAW had entered into a technology transfer agreement with Spain's Hispano Carrocera S.A. for the transfer of large coach body technology to the new company and with France's Renault V.I. for chassis and rear axle technology.
TIBS said it signed a formal Heads of Agreement with DAW for the joint venture on Wednesday.
Under the agreement, the partners would conduct a feasibility study for the joint venture, which was expected to be finalised by November 1996.
"The joint venture contract is expected to be signed before the end of 1996," TIBS said.
